prompt_demand: Outline the causal chain by which bile aids fat digestion: emulsification into droplets, larger surface area, faster lipase action, while bile itself is not an enzyme.
reason: The three marks require a linked mechanism (emulsify, so surface area rises, so lipase acts faster), which is a taught explanation rather than recall of a single fact; comparable mechanism items here (3-324 PROC, 3-331 WHY, 3-337 WHY) are Understand. AO1 and command word are correct.
uncertainty: medium; if the bank deliberately keeps all FEATURE-subtype cards at Remember for recall of a rehearsed sequence, Remember is defensible and this can be dropped.

prompt_demand: Process supplied mean root lengths from a controlled phosphate-deficiency investigation (calculate the 4.8 cm difference) and state and explain the supported conclusion.
reason: The demand (quote the difference in means from a controlled investigation and draw a conclusion) is structurally the same as 3-242 and 3-261, which are labelled AO3 as interpretation of investigation results (C4). B is defensible because the second mark asks for a reasoned explanation using DNA/ATP knowledge (B5), so keep, but the inconsistency with 3-242 should be noted.
uncertainty: medium; if the operator wants all 'conclusion from a controlled investigation' items treated as C, this would move to AO3 for consistency with 3-242.

prompt_demand: Use described seedling results (iron added at week 2, plants turn green versus pale matched controls) to judge which treatment is supported and link it to chlorophyll formation.
reason: Interpreting the outcome of a controlled treatment comparison sits on the B4/B5 versus C4 boundary (drawing conclusions from investigation results). B is defensible because the learner must infer cause from supplied information and explain it, so keep.
uncertainty: medium; a consistent rule that investigation-result conclusions are C would move it to AO3.

prompt_demand: Apply limiting-factor reasoning to explain why CO2 enrichment raises photosynthesis in a well-lit greenhouse but not a dim one.
reason: Greenhouse CO2 enrichment and limiting factors are taught content (A4), so A is defensible; the two-situation contrast does call for applying the limiting-factor idea, which makes AO2/Apply a reasonable alternative.
uncertainty: medium; if the dim versus well-lit contrast is judged to be a new situation rather than a rehearsed one, AO2/Apply would fit better.

prompt_demand: Explain why equal energy needs do not imply equal iron needs when one adult has menstrual blood loss.
reason: The reasoning (energy and iron are separate needs; blood loss removes haemoglobin iron) is close to the taught CHAIN account in 3-289, and its first guidance point is almost word for word the same as 3-306, which is labelled AO1. Separating two needs in a matched-comparison scenario is a defensible B inference, so keep.
uncertainty: medium; if the operator judges the matched-adult framing to be taught reproduction, AO1/Understand would match 3-306.

prompt_demand: Explain why enough food energy does not prevent scurvy: energy and vitamin C are different nutrients.
reason: This is a taught distinction (energy versus micronutrient, scurvy cause), so A is right; it is listed only because it shares its reasoning with 3-290 (AO2), and the two labels should be read together.
uncertainty: low for AO1; only relevant if 3-290 is relabelled.

prompt_demand: Infer that changing to seated duties with unchanged intake causes an energy surplus stored as fat.
reason: The energy-balance account is taught (compare 3-304 WHY, AO1), but the learner must infer the change in expenditure from the job change and link it to unchanged intake over time, which is a modest B7 everyday problem. Keep.
uncertainty: medium; a reviewer who sees this as a rehearsed energy-balance account would label it AO1/Understand.
